goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported feed HTML is stored as raw_html without sanitization, allowing a compromised feed to persist executable markup in every rendered topic/embed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and in app/models/post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. The imported content from RSS feeds (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) or remote URLs (import_remote method) is passed through without HTML sanitization, allowing potentially malicious markup to be stored and rendered. This is a security vulnerability where compromised feeds could inject executable content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every cache miss enqueues before validating embed_url, so forged requests with unique invalid URLs can grow the job queue without bound.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the embed_controller.rb code, the `best` action at line 8-17 shows that when `topic_id` is nil (cache miss), it enqueues a job at line 14 with `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The `ensure_embeddable` filter only validates the referer host matches `embeddable_host`, but doesn't validate the `embed_url` parameter itself. An attacker from a valid referer could send many requests with unique invalid embed_urls, each causing a job to be enqueued. The TopicRetriever does have some validation (checking embeddable_host matches URL host), but this happens in the job, not before enqueueing. This allows queue growth from forged requests with unique URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — A blank embed_by_username raises on downcase after every valid-host cache miss, and the loading page keeps re-enqueuing the permanently failing retrieval.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 48-51, the fetch_http method calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking if embed_by_username is blank first. The `return if user.blank?` check comes AFTER the downcase call. If embed_by_username is blank/nil, calling `.downcase` on it will raise a NoMethodError. This is called from perform_retrieve (line 42) which is triggered on valid host cache misses. The loading.html.erb page auto-refreshes every 30 seconds, which would keep re-triggering this failing retrieval. This is a real bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Remote retrieval follows redirects without revalidating the destination host, so an allowed host can redirect workers to internal services.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security concern in the diff. Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the `import_remote` method uses `open(url).read` (via OpenURI) to fetch remote content. OpenURI by default follows HTTP redirects. The code validates the initial URL's host against `embeddable_host` in topic_retriever.rb's `invalid_host?` method, but if the allowed host returns a redirect to an internal service (e.g., 127.0.0.1, internal AWS metadata endpoints), the redirect will be followed without revalidating the destination. This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability where an attacker controlling content on an allowed host could redirect requests to internal services.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The public embed script silently requires `discourseUrl` to end in `/`, so a normal origin URL produces an invalid `https://hostembed/best` endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 7: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`. The code concatenates discourseUrl directly with 'embed/best'. If discourseUrl is 'https://host' (without trailing slash), the result would be 'https://hostembed/best' which is invalid. The code assumes discourseUrl ends with '/' but doesn't enforce or document this requirement. This is a real bug that would cause the embed functionality to fail if the URL doesn't have a trailing slash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — URL absolutization handles only root-relative paths, so ordinary relative links such as `images/photo.jpg` remain relative to the Discourse embed page and resolve incorrectly.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-70, the code only handles URLs that start with '/' (root-relative paths) via `href.start_with?('/')` and `src.start_with?('/')`. URLs like 'images/photo.jpg' (relative to current path, not starting with '/') would not be matched by these conditions and would remain unchanged, causing them to resolve incorrectly relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the original source URL. This is a real bug in the URL handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42 — The new controller spec requires a synchronous `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` call, but the controller now calls only `Jobs.enqueue`, so this test deterministically fails.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42, it sets up expectations that TopicRetriever.new returns a mock, and that mock's retrieve method is called. The controller code in embed_controller.rb:14 shows `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` is called when topic_id is nil. However, the test mocks TopicRetriever directly with `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. This test would actually pass because the mock expectations are set up - the test doesn't actually verify the real code path, it just verifies that IF TopicRetriever.new is called, it would work. But looking more carefully, the controller calls Jobs.enqueue, not TopicRetriever directly. The test's expectations for TopicRetriever would never be satisfied since the controller doesn't call TopicRetriever.new directly. However, this appears to be a test design issue where the test is incorrectly written to test the wrong thing, but the finding claims the test 'deterministically fails' which is accurate - the TopicRetriever expectations would fail since they're never called.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting every existing post to cook_method 1 marks legacy posts as raw HTML, bypassing the normal cooking and sanitization pipeline on subsequent cooks.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the migration in db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb, it sets default: 1. Looking at Post.cook_methods in app/models/post.rb, the Enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which means :regular = 1 and :raw_html = 2 (Enum starts at 1 by default in Discourse). So defaulting to 1 means existing posts are marked as :regular (normal cooking), NOT raw_html. The finding incorrectly claims cook_method 1 is raw_html when it's actually the regular cooking method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table force: true can drop and recreate an existing topic_embeds table, destroying embed mappings during a rerun or partial-deployment recovery.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in the migration at line 3 will drop and recreate the table if it already exists. This is visible in the diff at db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb. While this is a valid concern for production deployments where the table might already exist with data, it's a design/architecture concern rather than a bug - migrations are typically run once in sequence. However, it could cause data loss in edge cases like partial deployment recovery or if the migration is re-run. This is a legitimate review concern but not a definite bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Changing this historical migration to create top_topics with force: true makes fresh or replayed migration runs silently drop any preexisting top_topics data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was modified to change 'create_table :top_topics do |t|' to 'create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|'. The 'force: true' option in Rails migrations causes the table to be dropped if it already exists before creating it. For a historical migration that may have already run in production, adding 'force: true' means if the migration is ever re-run (e.g., during database rebuild or in certain edge cases), it would silently drop all existing data in the top_topics table. This is a real data loss risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — Remove the unused `feed_key` method and its now-unnecessary Digest dependency, or wire it into polling as intended.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `feed_key` method is defined in poll_feed.rb (lines 20-22) but is never called anywhere in the file. The `poll_feed` method doesn't use `feed_key` at all. This is dead code that was likely intended to be used for caching/throttling (based on the pattern of creating a SHA1 hash of the URL) but was never wired in. The Digest require at line 4 is only used by this unused method. This is a legitimate code quality issue - unused code that should either be removed or properly integrated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — Move remote HTTP fetching and readability parsing out of the ActiveRecord model so persistence can be tested and evolved independently of transport concerns.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 44 in app/models/topic_embed.rb which contains the `import_remote` method that performs HTTP fetching via `open(url).read` and uses the ruby-readability library for parsing. This is a valid architectural concern - the method mixes HTTP transport concerns (fetching remote content) with ActiveRecord model responsibilities (persistence). The diff shows this method directly in the model class, making it harder to test persistence logic independently of network calls. This is a legitimate scope/architecture concern grounded in specific code in the diff, though it's a design preference rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:62 — Consolidate the duplicated anchor/image URL-rewrite loops into one selector-to-attribute mapping to prevent supported element handling from drifting.

adjudication.rationale: The finding suggests consolidating two loops that iterate over 'a' and 'img' elements to rewrite URLs. While this is a valid code style suggestion, it's purely a refactoring/style preference, not a bug or important non-bug issue. The two loops work correctly as written - they handle different elements (anchors and images) with different attributes (href and src). There's no actual defect, and the 'drift' concern is speculative. This is a minor code organization preference, not a substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The remote article body is read fully into memory with no size limit, so a large response can exhaust a worker's memory before parsing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code does `open(url).read` which reads the entire remote content into memory without any size limit. This is in the `import_remote` method. A malicious or misconfigured remote URL could return an extremely large response that would exhaust worker memory. This is a real security/reliability bug - there's no protection against large responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every cache miss reruns and fully imports the configured feed before fetching the article, so distinct embed URLs can repeatedly trigger work proportional to the entire feed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 35-45, the perform_retrieve method first checks if TopicEmbed exists, then if feed_polling_enabled? it runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which processes the entire RSS feed. This happens for every cache miss (every 60 seconds per URL). Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed iterates through all RSS items and calls TopicEmbed.import for each. So for each distinct embed URL that misses the 60-second throttle, the entire feed is re-polled and processed before fetch_http is called. This is inefficient - multiple concurrent requests for different embed URLs could each trigger full feed processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Remote article fetches have no open or read timeout, so an unresponsive embed host can occupy a worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 45-48, the import_remote method uses `open(url).read` without any timeout configuration. This is a real defect - if the remote server is slow or unresponsive, the worker thread will block indefinitely waiting for the response. The diff clearly shows this code being added with no timeout parameters passed to the open() call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — The throttle key is committed before retrieval succeeds, so a transient fetch failure causes the Sidekiq retry to return successfully without retrying the work.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with `setnx` and `expire` before `perform_retrieve` is called. The flow is: `retrieve` calls `retrieved_recently?` which sets the throttle key, then calls `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error in `fetch_http` or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), the throttle key remains set for 60 seconds. When Sidekiq retries the job, `retrieved_recently?` returns true because the key exists, causing the retry to skip the actual work. This is a real bug where transient failures prevent proper retry behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling retries means any transient feed failure or malformed item aborts the run and leaves all remaining updates stale until the next hourly poll.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set on line 12 of poll_feed.rb. This means if any exception occurs during feed processing (network error, malformed RSS, etc.), the job won't retry and all remaining items in the feed won't be processed until the next hourly poll. This is a legitimate architectural concern about the new code's resilience, though it's a design choice rather than a bug - the code works as written, but the choice to disable retries has real consequences for reliability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:134 — RSS and readability imports are stored as raw HTML without sanitization, allowing feed or page content to persist executable markup and trigger stored XSS for forum readers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that posts imported via RSS/readability use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (line 21 in topic_embed.rb), and in post.rb line 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. The imported content from external feeds (via ruby-readability or RSS) is stored and rendered as-is. While ruby-readability limits tags to a whitelist, the RSS feed content in poll_feed.rb uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which doesn't sanitize HTML. This raw HTML is then rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view (best.html.erb line 16), potentially allowing XSS from malicious feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:50 — The retriever validates only the initial URL host before open-uri follows redirects, so an open redirect on the embeddable host can turn this public flow into SSRF against another host.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. In topic_retriever.rb, the host validation at line 14 checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` only for the initial URL. Then in fetch_http (line 49), it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which in topic_embed.rb line 50 uses `open(url).read` via ruby's open-uri. The open-uri library follows HTTP redirects automatically. If the embeddable_host has an open redirect vulnerability, an attacker could craft a URL like `http://embeddable_host/redirect?to=http://internal-server/` which would pass the host check but then redirect to an internal server, enabling SSRF. This is a legitimate security concern in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25 — The public endpoint treats the spoofable Referer header as authorization, allowing unauthenticated clients to enqueue imports and create topics for arbitrarily many URLs on the configured host.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue in the embed_controller.rb. Looking at the ensure_embeddable method (lines 23-29), it checks `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` to validate access. The Referer header is easily spoofable by any HTTP client, so this is not a secure authorization mechanism. An attacker could set a fake Referer header matching the embeddable_host and then call the 'best' endpoint with arbitrary embed_urls, which would trigger `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (line 14) to import content from any URL on that host. This is a real security vulnerability where the authorization relies solely on a client-controlled header.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — The no-embed example expects synchronous TopicRetriever calls even though the controller now enqueues retrieve_topic, so this test fails instead of validating the new job boundary.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the embed_controller.rb shows that when no topic_id is found, it enqueues a job: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 sets up expectations like `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, expecting synchronous TopicRetriever calls. But the controller actually enqueues a job (Jobs::RetrieveTopic) which internally calls TopicRetriever. The test's expectations don't match the actual controller behavior - it expects direct TopicRetriever instantiation in the controller, but the controller enqueues a job instead. This is a real test bug where the test assertions don't match the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31 — PollFeed coverage only mocks poll_feed and never exercises feed parsing, link fallback, content handling, or TopicEmbed.import, leaving the entire import path unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the execute method's guard conditions and mocks poll_feed, never actually testing the poll_feed method itself which contains significant logic: RSS parsing with SimpleRSS, link/id fallback logic, content unescaping, and TopicEmbed.import calls. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial code in the diff (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 22-38).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — TopicRetriever tests stub private control-flow methods and never verify Redis throttling, existing-embed short-circuiting, feed fallback, or remote import behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the TopicRetriever tests in the diff (lines 1-46 of spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb) stub the private method `retrieved_recently?` and `perform_retrieve` rather than testing the actual implementation. Looking at the diff, the tests never verify: 1) Redis throttling logic in `retrieved_recently?` method, 2) the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` check in `perform_retrieve`, 3) the feed polling fallback path, or 4) the `fetch_http` remote import behavior. The tests only verify that `perform_retrieve` is called/not called under certain conditions, but don't test what `perform_retrieve` actually does. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic.
